title: fix(ci): the future-spec-major gate and the artifact-door pins stop moving with the version label
body:
Fixes #23135
Clause-②: no

The generated Version Packages PR #21988 (head `63eb607ad1`, spec label `18.0.0-next.0`) is red on four checks. Two of them are failures in their own right, and the other two are aggregators that roll those two up. Both real failures are pins on `main` that are stated against the spec package's version label, so they flip when the version pass rolls the label to 18, even though none of their own bytes changed. This PR fixes both on `main`, at their producers. It changes nothing on `changeset-release/main`, on #21988, in any release workflow or on any governed surface.

## Every red on #21988's current head

Read after the last of them completed at 2026-10-13T03:23Z: `GET /repos/objectstack-ai/objectstack/pulls/21988` returned head `63eb607ad15b883fee70224f20afbf3c89a18e46`, and `/commits/{sha}/check-runs` returned 44 runs: 32 success, 8 skipped, 4 failure, 0 still running. The five Test Core shards and `Type Check · workspace` that were running when the card was filed have all finished green, except shard 1 below.

1. **`Type Check · source gates`** (job 115105083441). Failing line: `✗ check-future-spec-major: 3 problem(s)`. This is **red 1** below.
2. **`TypeScript Type Check`** (the aggregator, job 115108695957). Failing line: ``type-check lane `typecheck-source-gates` concluded `failure` -- expected `success`.`` It has no failure of its own; it is red 1 rolled up.
3. **`Test Core (1/6)`** (job 115105339463). Failing line: `@objectstack/metadata:test: Tests 2 failed, 878 passed (880)`, plus `Failed: @objectstack/metadata#test` in the turbo summary. This is **red 2** below.
4. **`Test Core`** (the aggregator, job 115113050333). Failing lines: `Test Core: 1 of 6 declared shard(s) of test published no positive attestation (test-1-of-6).` and `Test Core: leg test reported result 'failure'`. It has no failure of its own; it is red 2 rolled up.

## Red 1: `check-future-spec-major` on the 18 tree

The three problems, verbatim, from the job and reproduced locally:

- `scripts/check-future-spec-major.mjs holds 10 citation(s) above the published major, below the floor of 12.`
- `QUOTATION_EXEMPTIONS entry 0 (docs/adr/0087-metadata-protocol-upgrade-contract.md, major 18) matched NOTHING`
- `QUOTATION_EXEMPTIONS entry 1 (docs/v17-docs-sweep.md, major 18) matched NOTHING`

### Does a prerelease of the next major count as published? Yes. The gate's own text decides it.

- The gate's header says: "refuses prose that dates a change to an `@objectstack/spec` npm major ABOVE the one this tree publishes". It also says: "The rule is 'an `@objectstack/spec` version whose MAJOR is above the major in `packages/spec/package.json`', read at runtime. A gate hardcoding `18` goes dormant the day the tree reaches 18".
- The gate's self-test has the row "the class is DERIVED — the same corpus is green once the tree reaches 18".
- The gate cites ADR-0087's level ruling: "A tombstone names the npm release it ships in, ⛔ never the protocol major."

The generated tree publishes `18.0.0-next.0`, which is an npm release of major 18 on the `next` dist-tag. On that tree, a citation of 18 names the release that carries the change, so it is legitimate there. Reading 18 as the published major is therefore correct, and this PR leaves the class itself (majors above the published one) exactly as it was.

### What was wrong: two pins stated against the label instead of against what they pin

- **The self-fixture floor** counted the gate's own citations `above spec.major`. The self-test fixtures cite 18 as "above 17", because they are written against a synthetic `17.4.0` manifest. At 18, those fixtures read as "at the major", so the floor saw a gutted instrument (10 of 12) although nobody had touched it. **Fix:** the floor now counts above `SELF_FIXTURE_MAJOR = 17`, the major the fixtures are written against. The two synthetic manifests now derive from that same constant.
- **The two `major: 18` quotation entries.** At 18, the sentences they excuse are legitimate citations. Such a citation is `continue`d before the ledger is ever consulted, so the entries matched nothing and the self-invalidation rule reported each one as a hole. An entry at or below the published major can excuse nothing: it is neither a hole nor over-broad. **Fix:** such an entry is now DORMANT. It is listed on the pass line ("delete once `main` itself carries that major") and is never judged. Live entries keep both refusals unchanged. The version branch cannot be edited, and `main` still needs these entries until it carries 18 itself, so a red there could never be fixed.
- `docs/adr/0087-metadata-protocol-upgrade-contract.md` is **not** edited. Entry 0 still points at it unchanged.

There are four new self-test rows (the roster floor moves from 29 to 33):

- the dormant-entry row;
- the floor at 18 is green;
- the gutted source is still red at 18;
- "the roll adds no problem — the REAL corpus one major up is never redder than at the published major". This row runs the real corpus, the real ledger and the real gate file a second time under a label shaped like the version branch's (major plus one, `.0.0-next.0`). It fails when that run reports more problems than the run at the published major. A tree only ever gains majors, and a citation that is legitimate at M is legitimate at M plus one, so the count can never rise unless some pin moves with the label. That is this card's class, and the row now catches it on `main`, before the roll reaches the version branch.

### Proofs

- **(a) Fails on the generated head, unmodified.** Fresh depth-1 clone of `changeset-release/main` at `63eb607ad15b883fee70224f20afbf3c89a18e46`, label `18.0.0-next.0`. `node scripts/check-future-spec-major.mjs --self-test` printed `✓ check-future-spec-major self-test: 29 cases pass.` (exit 0). `node scripts/check-future-spec-major.mjs` printed `✗ check-future-spec-major: 3 problem(s)`, the three lines above (exit 1).
- **(b) Passes there with the fix applied, uncommitted.** The same clone with this PR's file copied in (blob `dbe4fc5e0f`, identical to the committed one). The self-test printed `✓ check-future-spec-major self-test: 33 cases pass.`, with the roll row reading `(0 at 18, 0 at 19.0.0-next.0)` (exit 0). The gate printed `✓ check-future-spec-major: no @objectstack/spec citation names a major above 18`, then `3 live witnessed ledger entr(y|ies)`, then `2 DORMANT ledger entr(y|ies) at or below major 18 … docs/adr/0087-metadata-protocol-upgrade-contract.md (major 18), docs/v17-docs-sweep.md (major 18)` (exit 0).
- **(c) `main` stays green.** Worktree at `f7ec15171`: the self-test printed 33 cases pass, with the roll row reading `(0 at 17, 0 at 18.0.0-next.0)`, and the gate printed `no … citation names a major above 17`, `5 live witnessed ledger entr(y|ies)`. `pnpm check:future-spec-major` exited 0.
- **One-off mutations on `main`, restored.** Each mutation went through `node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` in WRAP mode, with my own EXIT/INT/TERM trap on absolute paths. Each restore was proven by blob equal to HEAD and `git diff HEAD` empty.
  - M1 put back the label-relative floor count (comparing `f.major` with `spec.major` again). The self-test went red on 3 rows; the roll row read `0 problem(s) at 17, 1 at 18.0.0-next.0 … holds 10 citation(s)`.
  - M2 deleted the dormancy line. The self-test went red on 2 rows; the roll row read `0 problem(s) at 17, 2 at 18.0.0-next.0`.
  - Together the two mutations reproduce, on `main`'s real corpus, exactly the three problems CI read on the version branch.

## Red 2: the two `plugin-artifact-forward-conversion.test.ts` failures

Verbatim, from the job and reproduced locally:

- "an artifact claiming the CURRENT spec version with a NON-default retired-key value still refuses with the tombstone": `AssertionError: expected 'expected "the strict parse must refus…' to contain 'allowRestore'`. The received message was `expected "the strict parse must refuse" not to be reached`.
- "…whose retired keys carry only the emitted default parses clean…": `AssertionError: expected [ Array(1) ] to have a length of +0 but got 1`.

### The producer is the test's fixture, not the conversion source

- The test claimed "the current surface" as `^` followed by the installed label. On the 18 tree that is `^18.0.0-next.0`. `parseRangeFloor` drops the prerelease tag, so the floor reads as `18.0.0`.
- A floor of `M.0.0` at or above the label is exactly where the door's **major-step half** opens. This is documented in the module doc of `packages/metadata-core/src/artifact-forward-conversion.ts` (verdict `converted-major-step`): a prerelease build of M may predate any retirement in step M, so every retired entry of step M is replayed. It is pinned at the labels `17.7.0`, `18.0.0-next.0` and `18.0.0` (`AT_OR_BELOW_THE_FLOOR`) in `packages/metadata-core/src/artifact-forward-conversion.test.ts`. `permission-allow-restore-purge-removed` has `toMajor: 18`, so at the roll the "current" artifact was converted on purpose, and both pins read that documented rescue as an amnesty.
- I probed the generated tree's own build of `@objectstack/metadata-core` with `applyArtifactForwardConversions`:
  - `{"installed":"18.0.0-next.0","range":"^18.0.0-next.0","verdict":"converted-major-step","authoredFloor":"18.0.0","notices":["permission-allow-restore-purge-removed","permission-allow-restore-purge-removed"]}`
  - against `{"range":"^18.0.1","verdict":"authored-current","notices":[]}`.
- A one-off mutation on `main` (label `17.7.0`), restored and proven as above, forced `'^18.0.0'` into both pins. It reproduced **both CI assertion texts verbatim** (`Tests 2 failed, 4 passed (6)`). So the M.0.0 floor alone is the mechanism, and the pins still go red when the window opens.

The source therefore behaves as designed, and the fixture's own comment was the false premise: "`^X.Y.Z` floors at exactly the installed version, so this pin survives every future spec release without edits" does not hold at any major's first release. **Fix:** the test now uses the floor derivation that the sibling `plugin-unbound-form-predicate-roots.test.ts` already uses for "the current surface": the first `x.y.z` past both the installed label and every retired entry's `retiredAfter`. That floor has a non-zero patch, so it is never an `M.0.0`. No assertion changed. One premise guard was added: the derived floor must be resolvable and have a non-zero patch.

### Proofs

- **(a) Fails on the generated head, unmodified.** In the same clone, after `pnpm turbo run build --filter='@objectstack/metadata^...' --filter='@objectstack/service-settings^...'` (15 of 15 tasks), `pnpm --filter @objectstack/metadata exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/plugin-artifact-forward-conversion.test.ts` printed `Tests 2 failed, 4 passed (6)`, with the two assertion texts above.
- **(b) Passes there with the fix applied, uncommitted.** Same command, this PR's file copied in (blob `a436ff248b`, identical to the committed one): `Test Files 1 passed (1)`, `Tests 6 passed (6)`.
- **(c) `main` stays green.** Worktree at `f7ec15171`: the file alone gave `Tests 6 passed (6)`; the whole package (`pnpm --filter @objectstack/metadata exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2`) gave `Test Files 61 passed (61)`, `Tests 880 passed (880)`; and `pnpm --filter @objectstack/metadata run typecheck` (`tsc --noEmit`) exited 0. `--listFiles` shows that the program does include this test file (61 test files in total).

### The other shard-1 ELIFECYCLE lines are collateral

`@objectstack/spec:test:repo`, `@objectstack/spec:test` and `@objectstack/service-settings:test` all end `ELIFECYCLE` between 03:00:06.39Z and 03:00:06.45Z. That is within 0.42 s of metadata's own `ELIFECYCLE`, and none of the three printed a failing test. Turbo's summary names only `Failed: @objectstack/metadata#test` (`Tasks: 37 successful, 42 total`). Run to completion on the generated tree (the clone, with this PR's two files present, neither of which those suites read for their verdicts), the suites measured as follows:

- `@objectstack/service-settings`: `Test Files 42 passed (42)`, `Tests 755 passed (755)`;
- `@objectstack/spec`, `--project repo`: `Test Files 57 passed (57)`, `Tests 997 passed (997)`;
- `@objectstack/spec`, `--project local`: `Test Files 660 passed (660)`, `Tests 20021 passed, 1 todo (20022)`.

## The pin

> after #21988 next refreshes from a `main` carrying this fix, every check on its head is green or an expected skip

The seat reads that run.

That refresh will also carry everything else that lands on `main` before it. The commits on `main` after this branch's merge base are outside what this PR measured.

## Local gates (CI runs the full farm)

I derived the gates with `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` on this branch at `f7ec15171`, after merging `origin/main` `d206d08ca`. It listed 73 commands. I ran each one and recorded its exit code before any pipe. `pnpm check:lean-entry-closure` first refused with `PREREQUISITE NOT MET` (no `packages/objectql/dist`); I built `@objectstack/objectql` and re-ran it, and it exited 0 (`2 published condition(s) measured from a real load`). `--ran` then reconciled the record as `73 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 72 run, 1 NOT-MEASURED (1 DERIVED from a recorded exit 3)`. All 72 that ran exited 0, including `pnpm check:future-spec-major`, `pnpm check:nul-bytes`, `pnpm check:cross-package-test-inputs`, `pnpm check:test-source-alias`, `node scripts/check-position-name-fold-loaders.mjs`, `pnpm check:type-check-coverage` and `pnpm check:type-check-debt`. `pnpm check:pm-dispatch-gates` ran detached and exited 0 (`1833 cases pass`, fast tier).

NOT MEASURED locally: `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads` (`PREREQUISITE NOT MET — this gate reads built output, and some package has no dist/`; it needs the whole workspace built, and 73 packages are unbuilt in this worktree). It reads built `dist/`, and this diff changes no built byte of any package, so it cannot move it. CI's lint jobs build and run it.

## Changeset

None: the `skip-changeset` label. The diff is a root `scripts/` file (the root package `@objectstack/spec-monorepo` is `private`) and a test file in `@objectstack/metadata`, whose `files` is `dist`, `README.md` and `CHANGELOG.md`. Grepping `packages/metadata/dist` for the new test helper `currentSurfaceFloor` finds 0 files, against a positive control `_parseAndRegisterArtifact` that finds 6.

## Acceptance notes

- **The two dormant entries can be deleted once `main` itself carries 18.0.0-next.N or later**, which happens after the maintainer lands the Version Packages PR. The gate's pass line names both from then on. Nobody currently owns that cleanup.
- **A related question, handed to the seat in the report and not acted on here:** while `main` sits in Changesets pre mode `next` with 24 `major` changesets queued, a change landing on `main` now first ships in `18.0.0-next.N`. The gate's prescription on `main` ("Not shipped yet ⇒ the bare published major, which ADR-0087 guarantees is the carrier (a pre-GA retirement ships `minor`)") still names 17. That is the same pre-mode family as #23042, which remains open, and it is a decision, not a fix for this card.
- The local `--project repo` run of `@objectstack/spec` took 20m24s under the shared lock on this 4-CPU container (`--maxWorkers=2`). This is a shared-box reading.
